rubric.title: Grade 9 English HL — Narrative Essay
rubric.subject: English Home Language
rubric.gradingNotes: Content carries the most weight. Structure and language are marked independently of content, so a strong story with weak punctuation still loses marks.

criteria.name: Content & Ideas
criteria.description: Original, convincing story with a clear focus and supporting detail.

criteria.name: Structure & Planning
criteria.description: Clear beginning, middle and end; paragraphs used purposefully.

criteria.name: Language & Style
criteria.description: Sentence variety, tone and register suited to a narrative.

students.name: Amara Nghidinwa
students.overallComment: A controlled, confident narrative. The opening image of the empty taxi rank does a lot of work in one sentence, and the ending earns its quietness instead of explaining itself.

criteria.name: Content & Ideas
criteria.evidence: The taxi rank was empty at six, but the smell of last night's rain still stood in the road.
criteria.comment: Original premise and a genuine emotional turn. One more concrete detail in the middle section would lift it to full marks.

criteria.name: Structure & Planning
criteria.evidence: By the time I reached the corner the rank was already behind me.
criteria.comment: Clean three-part shape. Paragraph breaks fall exactly where the scene shifts.

criteria.name: Language & Style
criteria.evidence: Quiet as a held breath, the morning waited for someone to need it.
criteria.comment: Good sentence variety and restraint. A few sentences start the same way in paragraph four.

criteria.name: Mechanics
criteria.evidence: The rank was empty it was always empty at six.
criteria.comment: Two comma splices in paragraph two; spelling and paragraphing otherwise secure.

students.name: Thabo Shikongo
students.overallComment: Energetic and readable. The dialogue carries the story, but the ending arrives suddenly and the reader is left without a sense of what changed.

criteria.name: Content & Ideas
criteria.evidence: The whole street knew before my mother did, and that was the worst part.
criteria.comment: Strong central conflict. The resolution is asserted rather than shown.

criteria.name: Structure & Planning
criteria.evidence: And then it was over.
criteria.comment: Good build-up; the final paragraph rushes the closing beat.

criteria.name: Language & Style
criteria.evidence: “You're not going,” she said, and the kettle kept boiling.
criteria.comment: Natural, believable dialogue. Narration occasionally slips into telling.

criteria.name: Mechanics
criteria.evidence: “sit down” she said
criteria.comment: Dialogue punctuation is inconsistent — several missing commas before speech tags.

students.name: Lena Amukoto
flags: Handwriting on page 2 was partly illegible — two sentences could not be read.
students.overallComment: A thoughtful piece with a strong sense of place. The middle section loses focus, and the handwriting on the second page made part of the argument impossible to follow.

criteria.name: Content & Ideas
criteria.evidence: The river carried the smell of the mill all the way to our gate.
criteria.comment: Vivid setting and a clear idea. Two sentences on page 2 could not be read, so the link between them was marked conservatively.

criteria.name: Structure & Planning
criteria.evidence: We walked. We walked some more. The sun moved.
criteria.comment: The middle section drifts; the ending returns to the main idea well.

criteria.name: Language & Style
criteria.evidence: Because the mill had closed, and because nobody had told the men, and because the trucks still came every Monday.
criteria.comment: Descriptive strength, but several long sentences lose their thread.

criteria.name: Mechanics
criteria.evidence: Its a long way to the river.
criteria.comment: Punctuation is generally sound where the writing is legible.

students.name: Kagiso Mbaenda
students.overallComment: A workable story told plainly. The idea is sound but the writing stays at the level of summary — the reader is told what happened rather than shown.

criteria.name: Content & Ideas
criteria.evidence: I was happy when I got the bicycle.
criteria.comment: Clear plot, limited detail. Little sensory description to hold the reader.

criteria.name: Structure & Planning
criteria.evidence: First we went to town. Then we went back. After that we went home.
criteria.comment: Logical order and sensible paragraphing.

criteria.name: Language & Style
criteria.evidence: It was nice. It was very nice. It was a nice day.
criteria.comment: Accurate but flat. Sentence lengths are very uniform.

criteria.name: Mechanics
criteria.evidence: we was walking home when the rain started
criteria.comment: Frequent tense shifts between past and present in paragraphs three and four.

students.name: Nangula Iipinge
flags: Only one page submitted — the guide expects a complete narrative, so Structure was capped.
Confidence is medium: the scanned page was rotated and partly cropped.
students.overallComment: An engaging opening that stops before the story develops. Marked on what was submitted, but a full draft would likely score considerably higher.

criteria.name: Content & Ideas
criteria.evidence: The bus was late again, and I had already counted the cars that went past.
criteria.comment: Promising premise, but the narrative ends mid-scene.

criteria.name: Structure & Planning
criteria.evidence: and then the bus came and
criteria.comment: No resolution present. Capped because the submitted work is incomplete.

criteria.name: Language & Style
criteria.evidence: I counted seventeen cars, one truck, and a dog that did not look at me.
criteria.comment: Confident voice in the opening paragraph.

criteria.name: Mechanics
criteria.evidence: i waited at the stop for two hours
criteria.comment: Hard to judge fully — the bottom of the page was cropped in the scan.

students.name: Petrus Kambwa
flags: The document appears to be a Grade 8 task, not the Grade 9 narrative essay.
Marked against the guide supplied, but the criteria may not match this paper.
students.overallComment: This looks like a different task. It was marked against the guide supplied, but the criteria do not line up cleanly with what was written, so treat these marks as provisional.

criteria.name: Content & Ideas
criteria.evidence: My holiday was good. We went to the beach and it was fun.
criteria.comment: Addresses a different prompt; relevance to the set topic is limited.

criteria.name: Structure & Planning
criteria.evidence: On the first day we swam. On the second day we swam. On the third day we swam.
criteria.comment: Organised, but around the wrong task.

criteria.name: Language & Style
criteria.evidence: The beach was nice and the water was nice and the food was nice.
criteria.comment: Simple sentences, limited development.

criteria.name: Mechanics
criteria.evidence: me and my brother went to the beach
criteria.comment: Frequent capitalisation errors at sentence starts.

students.name: Selma Uusiku
flags: Three pages were submitted but only page 1 could be read — pages 2 and 3 are out of focus.
Marked from page 1 only. Re-upload the full document before recording this mark.
students.overallComment: Only the first page was legible, so this mark reflects roughly a third of the submitted work. Do not record it without re-checking the document.

criteria.name: Content & Ideas
criteria.evidence: The first thing I remember is the sound of the gate.
criteria.comment: Only the opening is readable; the story cannot be assessed past page 1.

criteria.name: Structure & Planning
criteria.evidence: The gate, then the yard, then the door.
criteria.comment: Judged on page 1 alone.

criteria.name: Language & Style
criteria.evidence: It was loud. It is loud. It will be loud.
criteria.comment: Judged on page 1 alone.

criteria.name: Mechanics
criteria.evidence: the gate was old and it made a noise that i did not like
criteria.comment: Judged on page 1 alone.

students.name: Johannes Haufiku
students.overallComment: Assured writing with a genuinely surprising final line. The strongest control of sentence rhythm in the class.

criteria.name: Content & Ideas
criteria.evidence: My father's hands never once touched the paper he was signing.
criteria.comment: Original and fully realised. The central image is sustained without strain.

criteria.name: Structure & Planning
criteria.evidence: Then the letter came, and with it the noise.
criteria.comment: Tight, deliberate shape — every paragraph moves the story forward.

criteria.name: Language & Style
criteria.evidence: The house held its breath like a coin held edge-up.
criteria.comment: Excellent rhythm. One over-written simile in paragraph five.

criteria.name: Mechanics
criteria.evidence: I did not recieve the letter.
criteria.comment: Three spelling errors, all of the same word.
